strings: Deep in Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Maur Grimtotem lies dead. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent him to seek peace with the troggs, and his remains and satchel are still in the caverns.

Maur Grimtotem went into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar as an envoy to the troggs. Most of the Horde saw them as savage brutes beyond negotiation, but Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought peace might be possible, or at least said so. Maur carried her offer into the winding caverns. The troggs killed him, and his body remains under the watch of their chieftain, Oggleflint.

After Maur's death, Magatha sought adventurers to retrieve the satchel he carried into the caverns, as well as avenge him. Whether Maur believed peace with the troggs could be reached remains unknown. Those who find his belongings may still wonder whether Magatha sent him as a true envoy or as a pawn in her schemes.

Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings.

While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it.

Maurin directs most of his malice toward the Burning Blade cult entrenched across Desolace. He harbors utter disgust for their reckless ambition, mocking the cultists for failing to understand that their borrowed power merely binds them as thralls to their demonic masters. Through scrying spells and ritual knowledge, Maurin enlists Horde adventurers to systematically disrupt the cult's summonings and undermine their operations across the barren landscape.

Mebok Mizzyrix is an enterprising goblin entrepreneur residing in the port town of Ratchet. Ever eager to turn bizarre wilderness reagents into profit, he hires passing adventurers to gather unusual flora and fauna from across the Barrens and beyond. His most notorious project involves concocting a commercial intellect-enhancing beverage out of raptor horns.

Operating out of the bustling, neutral port of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic Steamwheedle spirit of relentless opportunism. While Ratchet caters to sailors, pirates, and merchants of all stripes, Mebok focuses his keen eye on Kalimdor's wilderness. Rather than mining standard ore or trading mundane cloth, he seeks out rare biological curiosities that he believes can be refined into highly lucrative concoctions and commodities.

Mebok's premier commercial endeavor is a proprietary 'smart drink' intended to artificially boost the intellect of whoever consumes it. Convinced that the natural cunning and ferocity of local raptors stems from the horns crowning their snouts, Mebok commissions hunters to harvest intact horns across the Barrens. To him, ethics and taste take a backseat to raw market potential, so long as paying customers believe the brew delivers results.

Beyond raptor-derived elixirs, Mebok maintains a constant demand for other bizarre specimens. From collecting volatile Deepmoss spider eggs to commissioning the retrieval of rare Blueleaf tubers buried deep within the brambles of Razorfen Kraul, his pursuits consistently push intrepid mercenaries into perilous territory. If an organism possesses strange properties, Mebok is certain there is a way to bottle and sell it.

Melithar makes no claim to a grand heritage and says nothing of his lineage. Whether he belongs to the Archdruid's family or shares an ancient Kaldorei name remains unknown. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender teaches warlocks from both factions the dark arts. The human warlock shares her knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft from a refuge in Kalimdor, far from orthodox authorities.

Menara Voidrender works from Ratchet, the neutral goblin port in the Barrens. Many warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms study in cellars or hidden slaughterhouses beneath their cities, but Ratchet keeps Menara away from the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, and Orgrimmar's overseers. There, she can pursue occult studies in plain sight. She teaches any capable apprentice, whatever their faction, making her a rare meeting point for practitioners of the dark arts.

Veteran conjurers know Menara as an authority on orbs that imprison and harness demonic spirits. She works with intricate reagents and guides apprentices through demanding rituals to make enchanted attire and binding implements. Her skill is known as far as Ironforge and the Undercity, and senior warlocks across Azeroth send their most promising students across the sea to seek her counsel.

Menara Voidrender shares an old history with Tabetha, a hermit mage living in deep isolation in the swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. Tabetha pursues the arcane, while Menara studies fel bindings and demonology. When powerful relics such as the Orb of Orahil need restoration or special knowledge, their shared past bridges the wilderness of Kalimdor.

Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant.

Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

Motega's peaceful research was upended when word arrived from Freewind Post that Arikara, a ferocious and legendary winged serpent spirit, had returned to the canyons seeking vengeance against Cairne Bloodhoof. Perplexed by why such a creature held a vendetta against the High Chieftain, Motega acted swiftly to protect the Horde. He instructed scouts to gather Incendia agave from the canyon basin and carry it to Elder Magatha Grimtotem in Thunder Bluff to be enchanted into a sacred powder. Using this preparation, hunters summoned and slew the serpent spirit, returning its hide to Whitereach Post as proof that Cairne was safe.

Arikara was not the only hazard challenging Motega's stay at Whitereach Post. Local Galak centaur continuously probed the camp, even scheming an assassination plot against Kanati Greycloud and his followers. To worsen matters, young Pao'ka wandered away from the safety of the campfire and vanished into the wyvern-infested heights of Highperch. Though frustrated by the young brave's thoughtlessness, Motega was immensely relieved when Horde travelers escorted the youth back alive.

Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor.

Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces.

Escaping human captivity, Doomhammer lived in hiding until he met Thrall, Durotan's orphaned son. Reinvigorated by the young shaman's vision, Orgrim rallied what was left of the orcish clans to storm the internment camps and break their people free. During a fierce battle at an encampment in the Arathi Highlands, the Warchief was struck down from behind by a lance. As he lay dying, he bestowed his black plate armor, his ancestral weapon—the Doomhammer—and the title of Warchief upon Thrall. In his honor, the liberated outpost was renamed Hammerfall, and the newly founded capital in Durotar was christened Orgrimmar.
